content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having an issue where some symbols on my webpage appear as question marks, such as the degree Celsius symbol. In the web editor, everything displays fine, so I suspect it's a text encoding issue. I'm unsure how to adjust the settings for correct display. Any advice is appreciated!

I've discovered that this problem happens when using HTTPS. When I switch to HTTP, all symbols, like degrees Celsius (the default unit in the web editor) and Czech letters, are displayed properly. If I use HTTPS, those symbols turn into question marks. Can someone explain why this happens? Thanks!
You should consider starting a support request.
Thanks for the suggestion! I've submitted a support request.

analysis.insight_summary: The user describes an issue where special characters, such as degree symbols and Czech alphabet letters, are replaced by question marks on their website when accessed via HTTPS. This rendering problem does not appear with HTTP, which suggests a compatibility or encoding issue with secure connections. The user is uncertain about where to change encoding and cannot resolve the display problem on their own.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants special characters and measurement units to be consistently and correctly displayed on their website, regardless of whether HTTP or HTTPS is used. They are looking for a straightforward way to adjust settings to fix encoding and display issues.
